content.title: Eric Stanley
content.text: Legendary actor and martial artist Chuck Norris has died at 86 years old. His family confirmed his passing on March 20, 2026. For years, he entertained audiences all around the world on his hit TV show "Walker, Texas Ranger." Chuck played a Texas Ranger, a law enforcement officer, and at the end of nearly every show he would catch the bad guys with his famous "roundhouse kick." You knew he would save the day and win every time. But there was something about his calm presence that pulled viewers in every single episode. He chose roles that stood for doing the right thing, setting a good example, helping other people, and having strong morals.Just days before his passing, Chuck shared a video celebrating his 86th birthday. He smiled, trained, and looked just like the man people had watched for years. He said, "I don't age. I level up." And Chuck was grateful for another year, good health, and the chance to keep doing what he loves. He thanked his fans and said their support meant more to him than they would ever know.When I was a kid growing up in the 90s, my grandma, who is also no longer here, would turn on Walker, Texas Ranger, and she would remind everyone in the house "Do not touch that TV, Chuck Norris is on." We watched Chuck together. And for many people, he was part of family time, someone kids looked up to, and he made people feel like everything was going to be okay, even if it was just for an hour. Please keep Chuck's family in your prayers. Thank you for all of the great life lessons and memories Chuck Norris. Rest in Peace.(Photo: The Norris Family)
